title: Restaurant Google Search acquisition
hypothesis: Independent and smaller multi-site restaurant operators actively searching for customer-feedback solutions will understand FlashFeedback's proposition, sign up through a predominantly self-service journey and reach real-world activation.
why_it_might_work: Tests both restaurant demand and whether high-intent search can support FlashFeedback's desired self-service acquisition model.
primary_success_signal: Restaurant businesses acquired through the experiment reaching first eligible genuine feedback.
supporting_signals: Measured signup → QR readiness → download/print/order → real opens → eligible genuine feedback.
notes: Current experiment: Google Search → /restaurants/ → signup → QR readiness/deployment signals → real feedback. Campaign: restaurants_search_test_01. Measurement limitations around pre-consent traffic remain documented separately.

title: Free Restaurant Feedback QR/Sign Generator
hypothesis: Restaurant operators searching for a customer-feedback QR code or sign will be more likely to adopt FlashFeedback if they receive an immediately useful artefact before being asked to create an account.
why_it_might_work: Combines acquisition, value demonstration, onboarding, QR creation and deployment; changes the value exchange from signing up for SaaS to receiving the thing they were looking for.
test_when: QR-related searches look commercially relevant; ads get clicks but signup conversion is weak; signups occur but QR setup/deployment is weak; or organic search reveals meaningful QR-tool intent.
primary_success_signal: Businesses acquired through the generator reaching first real customer feedback.
supporting_signals: Generator use → account creation → QR readiness/deployment → real feedback.
notes: Concept: Search/content → create free restaurant feedback QR sign → restaurant name/basic config → preview → Want to receive and track responses? Create your free FlashFeedback account → carry config into account/onboarding → QR already ready.

title: Restaurant QR Placement Guide
hypothesis: Restaurant operators searching for practical QR-placement guidance represent relevant acquisition traffic, while the guidance can simultaneously improve QR deployment among existing users.
why_it_might_work: One content asset may improve both discovery and activation.
test_when: QR placement appears in search terms; businesses prepare QRs but receive few opens; founder follow-up shows placement uncertainty; or organic acquisition becomes a priority.
primary_success_signal: Qualified acquisition and/or measurable improvement in QR deployment/first-feedback behaviour.
supporting_signals: Qualified organic visitors; deployment and first-feedback behaviour among guide readers.
notes: Working title: Where to Put Customer Feedback QR Codes in a Restaurant. Possible placements: tables, bill folders, till/counter, collection points, receipts, takeaway packaging, exit/customer-service moments.

title: Powered by FlashFeedback product-led referral loop
hypothesis: Some people submitting feedback through FlashFeedback are themselves business owners/decision-makers and may discover the product through the customer journey.
why_it_might_work: Existing customer scans may become distribution to other restaurants.
test_when: Customer-side scan volume becomes meaningful and enough businesses are actively deployed.
primary_success_signal: New activated businesses attributable to the customer feedback journey.
supporting_signals: Owner CTA impressions/clicks → attributable signups → activation.
notes: Existing context: FlashFeedback already has/had an Are you a business owner? CTA at the end of the feedback journey. Inspect production and existing analytics before changing it. Potential loop: Restaurant A → customer scans → owner CTA → customer owns/manages another business → Restaurant B signs up.

title: Demo-as-customer acquisition journey
hypothesis: Prospects will understand FlashFeedback faster if they experience the customer journey themselves before being asked to sign up.
why_it_might_work: Experiencing both sides can make the proposition concrete.
test_when: Landing traffic exists but visitors do not convert, or founder conversations show people do not immediately understand the product.
primary_success_signal: Improved signup and downstream activation among demo users.
supporting_signals: Demo completion → signup → genuine downstream activation.
notes: Concept: Experience FlashFeedback as your customer → rate → submit example feedback → immediately show what the restaurant would see → signup CTA. Keep demo feedback separate from genuine customer feedback.

title: YouTube and short-form problem-led content
hypothesis: Restaurant operators who are not actively searching for feedback software may engage with recognisable customer-experience problems through video.
why_it_might_work: Creates demand beyond existing high-intent searches.
test_when: High-intent search volume is limited, paid acquisition is unattractive, or demand creation is needed rather than demand capture.
primary_success_signal: Qualified traffic becoming activated FlashFeedback businesses, not video views.
supporting_signals: Qualified visits → signup → activation by content source.
notes: Themes: unhappy customer doesn't complain; five-second restaurant feedback; catch bad experience before the customer leaves; where to put feedback QR codes; feedback without long surveys; QR feedback vs Google reviews.

title: Free Restaurant Feedback Toolkit
hypothesis: A practical restaurant feedback deployment kit may attract relevant operators and reduce effort required to deploy FlashFeedback.
why_it_might_work: Useful physical materials can reduce deployment effort.
test_when: Deployment friction becomes a leading bottleneck.
primary_success_signal: Toolkit users reaching real QR deployment and feedback.
supporting_signals: Kit use/download → physical placement → real opens and feedback.
notes: Potential contents: table sign, counter sign, bill-folder insert, takeaway sticker format, QR placement guide, recommended wording. Prefer connecting to a FlashFeedback account rather than a detached generic PDF where possible.

title: Google Reviews vs Private Feedback content
hypothesis: Restaurant operators researching Google reviews/reputation management may have an adjacent need for private customer feedback.
why_it_might_work: Adjacent reputation-search demand may reveal relevant operators.
test_when: Search Console or Ads search terms reveal relevant review/reputation queries.
primary_success_signal: Qualified organic visitors becoming activated businesses.
notes: Potential content: Google review QR code vs private feedback QR code / Why Google reviews and private customer feedback do different jobs. Constraint: do not frame as review gating or negative-review suppression.

title: Competitor / alternative pages
hypothesis: Operators comparing existing products may represent high-commercial-intent traffic.
why_it_might_work: Comparison searches may find buyers already evaluating solutions.
test_when: FlashFeedback has enough credibility/customer evidence, Search Console/Ads reveal competitor searches, and restaurant validation is stronger.
primary_success_signal: Qualified comparison visitors becoming activated businesses.
notes: Examples: FlashFeedback vs ServiceRater / MoniVibe / TasteScore; Tattle alternatives for independent restaurants; restaurant feedback software for independent operators. Comparisons must be fair, current and evidence-based; verify named competitors before publishing.

title: Restaurant supplier / agency partnerships
hypothesis: Businesses already trusted by restaurant operators could distribute FlashFeedback more efficiently than direct paid acquisition.
why_it_might_work: Trusted suppliers can introduce a validated proposition at relevant moments.
test_when: Restaurant activation is proven, paid acquisition looks expensive, and there is enough evidence for partners to recommend it.
supporting_signals: Referrals → activated businesses per partner and acquisition effort.
notes: Potential partners: restaurant website agencies, menu designers/printers, hospitality marketing agencies, EPOS consultants, QR/NFC suppliers, independent hospitality consultants.

title: Restaurant-owner communities
hypothesis: Restaurant-owner communities can provide both problem discovery and qualified awareness without high-touch field sales.
why_it_might_work: Relevant conversations may improve discovery and create qualified awareness.
test_when: Useful during early discovery, especially if search demand is limited.
primary_success_signal: Repeated problem evidence and qualified community visitors becoming activated businesses.
supporting_signals: Concrete operator experiences; qualified visits and activation.
notes: Contribute genuinely. Explore how operators learn about bad experiences, whether diners scan table QRs, where they place prompts, and what feedback they act on.

title: New vertical landing-page experiments
hypothesis: The core private-feedback mechanism may solve similar problems in other in-person businesses.
why_it_might_work: Restaurant learning may transfer to comparable physical customer moments.
test_when: Restaurant learning clarifies which value proposition/product behaviour transfers.
primary_success_signal: Activation within the new segment, not traffic.
supporting_signals: Segment-specific signup → deployment → first genuine feedback.
notes: Potential segments: cafés, pubs, salons, gyms/studios, clinics/dentists, local services. Do not create pages just for SEO.

title: POS / app marketplace distribution
hypothesis: Integrations may eventually generate feedback opportunities automatically and expose FlashFeedback to businesses through existing software ecosystems.
why_it_might_work: Integration value may come from automatically creating feedback opportunities, not just importing metadata.
test_when: Restaurant proposition is validated, manual QR deployment limits growth/response volume, a specific platform shows target-market penetration, and integration effort is justified.
primary_success_signal: Activated businesses and genuine feedback opportunities attributable to the platform.
supporting_signals: Target-market adoption × automatic feedback reach × context richness × distribution leverage ÷ implementation/commercial complexity.
notes: Strategic/later. Do not build an integration just because enterprise competitors have one.
